title: POC Week 6 - Stakeholder & Economic Signoff
summary: Final weekly sync for the 6-week POC. Reviewed end-to-end results, latency/cost tradeoffs, and business case numbers. Stakeholders signaled readiness to move to pilot/contract pending pricing and a short production validation run. Agreed owners and timeline for paperwork, SOC2 docs, and a 48h benchmark on dedicated capacity.
topics: Tuning changes and model variant choices
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood): Thanks everyone for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in, we'll try to keep to 45 minutes but planned for about 50. Quick roll call.
[00:12] Priya Kapoor (NorthBridge): Priya here - head of ML.
[00:16] Tom Ellison (NorthBridge): Tom - CTO.
[00:20] Marco Diaz (NorthBridge): Marco - Product.
[00:22] Leah Simmons (NorthBridge): Leah - Finance.
[00:25] Amit Patel (NorthBridge): Amit - SRE.
[00:28] Jonah Park (Redwood SE): Jonah - solutions.
[00:30] Asha Rao (Redwood CSM): Asha - CSM.
[00:34] Maya: Cool. Agenda: quick results recap, what we tuned in week 6, business case numbers Leah walked us through last week, then signoff ask and next steps.
[01:10] Priya: I'll start - the accuracy numbers held up after the prompt engineering and we didn't see drift across the 25k sample set, so that's good. there were a couple of outliers where the model hallucinated on older docs.
[01:35] Jonah: Right, we added the prefix caching and increased the KV cache retention for those long context examples which reduced those hallucination spikes by about 18 percent in our internal evals - note: KV cache transcription sometimes shows up as K V cash in the notes.
[02:05] Marco: The latency numbers - can someone restate the p95 on hosted vs dedicated? last sheet showed hosted p95 360ms, dedicated p95 120ms?
[02:18] Maya: Yes, hosted at your account's pattern was ~350-380ms p95 on the 2k token median sequences. On our dedicated pool with q4_0 quant + batching the p95 dropped to 110-130ms depending on load.
[02:45] Amit: Understood, but what's the cost delta per 1M tokens? Leah we had last week's calc but can you summarize?
[02:55] Leah: Sure - on hosted it's roughly $2.1k per 1M tokens (including egress/overhead), dedicated amortized (with reserved commit assumptions) is about $1.2k per 1M tokens. So roughly 40-45% cost savings at our projected volume. That's before additional savings from smarter batching.
[03:25] Tom: That's significant. My only risk flag is operational: will we get the same p95 under production traffic patterns, bursty spikes, and multi-tenant interference?
[03:40] Jonah: Good callout, we ran mixed-traffic injection tests in week 5, and the dedicated pool isolate reduced tail latency variance - but we still want to run a 48 hour production-like validation in your VPC to confirm. That was the ask in the docs.
[04:00] Priya: On model variant - we tuned between redwood/small-opt and redwood/medium-quant. The small-opt is cheaper but has a 3-4% drop in classification recall on edge cases. We think medium-quant is the best balance.
[04:20] Marco: Did you try dynamic routing? sending critical queries to medium and other to small?
[04:25] Jonah: Yes, we prototyped policy routing by confidence score; it shaved 12% off cost while keeping recall almost flat. The rule is: if confidence <0.7 route to medium-quant. It adds a tiny routing latency but saves cost.
[04:45] Leah: Economically that policy looks attractive. If we project 2M tokens/month, the blended cost lands near $1.35k/M token.
[05:05] Maya: Great. I'd like to capture the signoff ask - we need stakeholder alignment to proceed to reserved capacity pilot and contract. Leah, does that make sense from finance?
[05:18] Leah: Yes, but we'll need committed terms and the pricing tiers in writing. Also request a cap on data egress line item for the contract.
[05:30] Tom: Security ok? We got the SOC2 docs last week but need the architecture diagram for private VPC deployment for our InfoSec review.
[05:40] Asha: We'll attach the VPC diagram and the dataflow sheet; Jonah can also do a 30 minute InfoSec walkthrough.
[05:47] Amit: For SRE we need logs retention settings and support runbook for failover - and a contact for on-call during the 48h validation.
[05:58] Jonah: I'll be the primary escalation for the validation and will share the runbook and a short playbook for failover procedures.
[06:10] Priya: Ok I want to bring up a small transcription-y detail - the model underestimates tokenization on long HTML inputs, so cost for some docs could spike. Has tokenizer normalization been applied?
[06:28] Jonah: Yes we applied pre-tokenization normalization and trimmed long HTML to text with the sanitizer rules. There remain a small percentage of malformed pages though. We flagged those in the results sheet (link: https://redwood.company/poc/nba/results-week6).
[06:50] Maya: Quick check: any vendors still in consideration that would materially change the economics?
[06:57] Tom: We're looking at an internal homegrown option and briefly at Bedrock, but the team prefers Redwood for the runtime optimizations and the trial numbers.
[07:10] Leah: I will still need a line item comparison that includes estimated infra ops for the internal build.
[07:20] Maya: We'll provide a simple 3-way cost comparison.
[07:25] Marco: Can we move to the ask about signoff criteria - Priya, from ML is the list accurate?
[07:32] Priya: Items for signoff - 1) production-like 48h run with p95 within 15% of dedicated numbers, 2) no accuracy regression >1% on the eval benchmark, 3) runbook and SOC2 artifacts provided, 4) pricing and reserved terms accepted by finance. If those are green I recommend go-ahead.
[08:00] Jonah: We'll outline the validation plan: scheduled 48h run (we recommend off-peak start), traffic replay of your production traces, and automated monitors for latency/accuracy/cost. We'll stream logs to your S3 and provide Grafana dashboards.
[08:25] Amit: For the logs stream, can we anonymize PII? We have to ensure we don't land customer PII in Redwood logs.
[08:33] Asha: By default the POC used redaction and we can confirm the retention window. We'll provide the redaction config.
[08:45] Leah: On the contract, finance needs the effective date and the SLA credits terms spelled out.
[08:54] Maya: We'll include those in the draft.
[09:02] Marco: Any open technical risks?
[09:05] Jonah: Only known item is long-tail malformed docs and a small set of edge-case prompts that increase context window usage; we have mitigations (sanitizer + prefix caching + TTL for KV).
[09:20] Tom: Alright let's talk timeline - if we lock pricing this week can we run the 48h validation next week?
[09:30] Maya: Yes, we can start the validation as early as Tuesday 2025-06-10, pending paperwork and VPC access.
[09:38] Leah: Finance can sign the term sheet conditionally, we need the exact numbers and a 30 day cancellation clause for the pilot.
[09:46] Maya: Noted.
[09:48] Priya: I also want to confirm monitoring for model drift - can Redwood alert on regression against a baseline prompt set?
[09:56] Jonah: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports prompt set evals and can trigger regression alerts and performance baselines. We'll enable that for the pilot.
[10:08] Marco: Any dev portal or API key rotation things we need to do?
[10:12] Asha: We'll provide short-lived keys for the validation and rotate them after the run.
[10:18] Leah: One more finance question: if the pilot shows the expected savings, what's the expected lead time to convert to a committed reserved capacity?
[10:25] Maya: Typically 2-4 weeks after pilot and legal review. We can accelerate with a signed term sheet.
[10:32] Tom: Ok.
[10:35] Maya: Quick pivot - Jonah can you summarize the week 6 tuning we did that materially changed the numbers?
[10:42] Jonah: We switched the default quant profile to q8_0 for non-critical routes, tuned the batching windows from 25ms to 40ms for better throughput, and enabled prefix cache hot keys for repeated conversation starts. That reduced token spend by ~9% in our sim and improved p95 on dedicated by ~10ms.
[11:10] Priya: The precision/recall tradeoff looked safe. Good.
[11:20] Marco: Back to signoff - Leah, are you comfortable signing conditional on the 48h run?
[11:27] Leah: Yes conditional signoff. I need the term sheet and invoice estimate by Thursday 2025-06-05.
[11:36] Maya: We'll get that to you.
[11:40] Tom: For the 48h we'd like a support window with someone on-call, Jonah you said you'll be primary - what hours?
[11:47] Jonah: I'll be available 8am-6pm your timezone and provide escalation contacts for nights.
[11:55] Amit: We'll need to test failover in the run and confirm TTLs on KV cache are behaving as expected under replica failover.
[12:05] Jonah: We'll include a failover scenario in the test plan.
[12:12] Maya: Any blockers to proceed?
[12:14] Priya: None from ML.
[12:16] Tom: Security wants the VPC diagram and a 30 min call.
[12:20] Asha: We'll schedule InfoSec call for Monday 2025-06-09.
[12:25] Leah: Finance will review term sheet Thursday and aim to return approvals by Friday.
[12:30] Maya: Great. Let's wrap with explicit action owners.
[12:35] Jonah: I'll read them out.
[12:40]
